source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
3. Identify the reporting period for which you are documenting the losses.
4. Conduct a comprehensive internal audit to ensure all reported financial information is accurate and up-to-date.
5. Segregate the various types of losses (e.g., operational, financial, legal, or due to asset impairment).
6. Use the accrual method of accounting to recognize losses when they occur, not when they are actually paid.
7. Ensure losses are recorded in the correct general ledger account according to the chart of accounts.
8. Review and apply relevant Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) to account for the loss.
9. Calculate any impairment losses on assets, using appropriate valuation methods and concepts.
10. Document any loss due to discontinued operations separately and in accordance with the relevant accounting standards.
11. Acknowledge and account for any extraordinary losses (like those due to natural disasters or changes in laws).
